instructions:
1. Set the suspension handles to about chest height and stand facing away from the anchor.
2. Grip a handle in each hand, arms extended in front at shoulder height, and lean forward with a straight body from head to heels.
3. Brace your core and open your arms out to the sides with a slight elbow bend, lowering your chest toward the handles.
4. Drive through your chest to bring your arms back together in front of you.
5. Keep your hips level and avoid rotating the torso.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Step your feet back to increase difficulty and forward to make it easier.
2. Keep a steady slight bend in the elbows throughout.
3. Exhale as you press the handles together, inhale as you open the arms.
4. Keep the core tight to stop the hips from sagging.

instructions:
1. Set the suspension handles to about knee height and place the top of one foot in a handle behind you.
2. Stand tall on the front leg with your torso upright and core braced.
3. Bend the front knee to lower until the front thigh is roughly parallel to the floor.
4. Keep the front knee tracking over the toes and the chest up.
5. Drive through the front heel to return to standing.
6. Finish all reps, switch legs, and repeat.
tips:
1. Keep most of your weight on the front leg, not the suspended foot.
2. Control the descent to manage the instability.
3. Exhale as you drive up, inhale as you lower.
4. Keep your front shin near vertical to protect the knee.

instructions:
1. Set the suspension handles to about knee height and lie on your back with both heels in the handles, legs extended.
2. Place your arms by your sides for support and brace your core.
3. Lift your hips off the floor to form a straight line from shoulders to heels.
4. Bend your knees to pull your heels toward your glutes while keeping the hips high.
5. Slowly extend your legs back to the straight starting position.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips lifted throughout so the hamstrings stay loaded.
2. Move with a slow, controlled tempo to manage the instability.
3. Exhale as you curl, inhale as you extend.
4. Squeeze your glutes to hold the bridge instead of arching your lower back.

instructions:
1. Set the suspension handles to about knee height and sit on the floor with both heels in the handles, legs extended.
2. Place your arms by your sides for support and brace your core.
3. Lift your hips off the floor while keeping your legs straight.
4. Pull your knees toward your chest, stopping just short of contact.
5. Slowly extend your legs back to the starting position.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core braced to stop your lower back from arching.
2. Start with a smaller range and increase it as control improves.
3. Exhale as you tuck the knees in, inhale as you extend.
4. Move slowly to keep the suspended legs steady.

instructions:
1. Set the suspension handles to about waist height and stand facing the anchor.
2. Grip the handles with palms facing down and lean forward with a straight body from head to heels.
3. Bend your elbows to bring your hands toward your forehead, keeping the upper arms still.
4. Brace your core and press through your hands to extend the elbows fully.
5. Slowly bend your elbows to return to the starting position.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Step your feet forward to make it harder and back to make it easier.
2. Keep the upper arms fixed so only the elbows move.
3. Exhale as you extend, inhale as you bend.
4. Keep the core tight to hold the body in a straight line.
